description: Fleet session-management Phase B, D1+D2 (§4). Validates role_class (ephemeral | project | principal — primary/chat are never spawn-assigned), work_class, and budget_line; when role_name is given, checks the fill-never-mint rule for principal offices (role_not_legislated when no role row exists yet) and the reserved <solet>-Main mint guard (reserved_role_name). Writes the managed_session ledger row in 'spawning' state BEFORE resolving and dispatching through the host driver, so a half-failed spawn stays visible rather than silently disappearing. Three host drivers ship: 'operator' (degenerate, observes via registration only, never spawns), 'headless' (D1 — spawns an actual Claude Code process over stream-json, config-gated fail-closed on a resolved permission mode/.mcp.json/the claude binary), and 'tmux' (D2 — spawns a detached tmux session running the interactive claude CLI, config-gated fail-closed on the tmux binary/version plus the same claude-launch checks as headless; its spawn() also runs a bounded PTY-confirm expect loop for the interactive --dangerously-load-development-channels prompt, fail-closed on timeout). Host choice affects deploy survival: a 'headless' worker is swap-mortal by construction (a direct child of the platform process, killed unconditionally on every platform stop including a blue-green deploy's quiesce step) while a 'tmux' worker is swap-durable by construction (its pane belongs to the independent tmux daemon, untouched by the platform's stop/swap path) — prefer 'tmux' for any worker expected to outlive a single release; a deploy holding live headless workers needs an explicit quiesce-or-accept decision recorded in the deploy reason. A spawn-time PreToolUse tool allowlist mechanism exists (allowed_tools, or resolved per-work_class from plugin.yaml's work_class_tool_allowlists) — an out-of-allowlist tool call is denied with a clean error, never executed and never a silent hang — but per operator ruling (2026-08-03, 'we don't have any restrictions now') it ships UNARMED by default: an empty/unconfigured allowlist means no extra restriction, not a lockdown. The permission mode itself (plugin.yaml's headless_permission_mode) similarly accepts any value today; the driver only refuses when no mode resolves at all. The tmux driver denies Claude Code's structured-choice AskUserQuestion tool by default (operator ruling, 2026-08-14 — its blocking picker stalls an unattended or peer-driven session); allow_askuserquestion=true lifts the deny for that one spawn. The headless driver needs no equivalent: measured live, its stream-json mode never enumerates the tool in the first place, so the flag is inert there. The codex runtime has no equivalent tool at all.
embedding_description: Spawn a new fleet-managed session (ephemeral, project, or principal role class) with a lane, work class, and budget line, writing its lifecycle ledger row before dispatching it through the declared host driver (operator, headless, or tmux). Distinct from list_sessions (read the fleet roster) and session_status (read one session's row).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_instance_id (the new session's identity), host (the resolved driver), host_ref (the driver's spawn handle), lifecycle_state (the ledger row's current state — 'spawning' on a request still in flight, 'terminated' if the dispatch itself failed synchronously), first_turn_source ('charter' if a lane_charter row was on file for this lane and its text was driven as turn 1, 'fallback' if a fixed bootstrap acknowledgement was driven instead), first_turn_delivered (whether that first-turn send actually succeeded — a driver-channel fault here never blocks the spawn itself), and first_turn_error (non-empty detail when first_turn_delivered is false, empty on success).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: State the new agent_instance_id and which host it was dispatched to. If lifecycle_state is 'terminated', make clear the spawn did NOT succeed — read the error for why, not this field alone. If first_turn_delivered is false, say so explicitly and surface first_turn_error, worded per runner: a Claude watch-transport worker with no delivered first turn cannot arm its Stop-hook wake loop; a managed Codex worker has no Stop-hook wake loop to arm at all (stock Codex does not execute async command hooks) and depends on its host driver / drive_on_delivery instead. Either way, first_turn_delivered=false means the worker stays unreachable at zero token cost until someone drives it manually.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validation runs BEFORE the ledger write (unknown_role_class, unknown_work_class, budget_line_required, role_not_legislated, role_class_conflict, reserved_role_name) so a refused spawn never touches state. Host resolution errors (host_not_declared, host_mechanism_missing) also precede the write. host_cannot_spawn is the one failure that happens AFTER the ledger row exists — the row is transitioned straight to 'terminated' before the error surfaces, so no spawn is ever left stuck in 'spawning' for a dispatch already known to have failed.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: unknown_role_class/unknown_work_class: the caller passed a value outside the declared taxonomy. budget_line_required: budget_line was empty. role_not_legislated: role_class='principal' named a role_name with no existing role row — principal offices are fill-never-mint, not mintable through this verb. role_class_conflict: role_name already exists under a DIFFERENT role_class than requested. reserved_role_name: role_name matches the <solet>-Main pattern and has no legislated row yet. host_not_declared: an explicit blank host override was passed. host_mechanism_missing: the resolved host (override, FLEET_SESSION_HOST env, or the 'headless' default) has no driver registered in this build at all — none of 'operator'/'headless'/'tmux' matched, most likely a typo'd host name. host_cannot_spawn: the resolved driver is registered but cannot spawn right now — the 'operator' driver never spawns (degenerate by design), or the 'headless'/'tmux' driver is registered but unconfigured (missing permission mode / .mcp.json / the claude binary, or for tmux an unsupported tmux version — the error names exactly which).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For role_not_legislated, legislate the office first via plugin::agent_messaging_plugin::legislate_role (role_class='principal'), or spawn with role_class='project' instead. For host_mechanism_missing, pass a host name that is actually registered ('operator', 'headless', or 'tmux') — there is no other name to wait for; check for a typo. For host_cannot_spawn against 'headless' or 'tmux', fix the exact configuration gap the error names (permission mode, MCP config, the claude binary, or the tmux binary/version); against 'operator', launch the session manually instead — this verb cannot do it for that driver.
